framework.definition: Takes responsibility for team commitments, decisions and outcomes, and enables team members to deliver rather than doing everything personally.
keyBehaviours: Supports employees without taking over their work.
Escalates risks with facts and possible solutions.

framework.definition: Recognises and manages personal emotions and remains calm, respectful and constructive during pressure, setbacks and disagreement.
keyBehaviours: Recognises the impact of personal behaviour.
Acknowledges mistakes and takes corrective action.

framework.definition: Learns from experience and feedback and adjusts the managerial approach according to the situation and employee needs.
keyBehaviours: Changes approaches that are not effective.

framework.definition: Converts team requirements into clear goals, priorities, responsibilities and realistic timelines.
keyBehaviours: Explains what needs to be achieved.
Distinguishes important work from urgent work.
Allocates work based on capability and workload.• Reviews progress against milestones.

framework.definition: Assigns work with clear expectations, appropriate authority and suitable review while allowing employees to take ownership.
Understands day-to-day team problems, considers relevant information and makes timely and practical decisions.
Sets clear performance expectations, monitors progress, recognises effective work and addresses performance gaps consistently.
keyBehaviours: Clarifies expected results, standards and timelines.

framework.definition: Provides timely, specific feedback and uses questions and guidance to help employees improve their performance.
keyBehaviours: Gives feedback close to the relevant event.
Explains the impact of behaviour or performance.

framework.definition: Understands employee strengths and development needs and provides suitable opportunities for learning and growth.
keyBehaviours: Identifies employee strengths and capability gaps.

framework.definition: Communicates information, expectations and decisions clearly and listens actively to understand employee views and concerns.
keyBehaviours: Explains the purpose and context of work.
Conducts purposeful team and one-to-one discussions.

framework.definition: Builds respectful and dependable relationships and treats team members consistently, ethically and fairly.
keyBehaviours: Provides fair access to work and development opportunities.

framework.definition: Addresses disagreements, behavioural concerns and sensitive issues directly, calmly and respectfully.
keyBehaviours: Focuses on behaviour rather than personality.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: Is beginning to understand responsibility for team outcomes but continues to depend considerably on senior-manager direction, particularly when decisions are difficult or delivery is at risk.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Completes personal responsibilities.
Hesitates to make decisions.
May avoid addressing delivery gaps.
May take work back from employees.
Developing.watchOuts:
Avoiding difficult decisions.
Blaming circumstances.
Escalating routine issues.
Retaining excessive control.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Takes responsibility for routine team commitments and follows through in familiar situations, although confidence and consistency may reduce when outcomes are uncertain or at risk.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Provides basic direction.
Monitors delivery.
Takes action on routine issues.
May seek excessive support during setbacks.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
Late escalation.
Inconsistent follow-through.
Defensiveness when results are poor.
Focusing on explanations instead of action.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Consistently owns team commitments, decisions and outcomes while enabling employees to take responsibility for their own work and resolve appropriate issues independently.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Addresses issues without blame.
Makes decisions within authority.
Escalates risks with facts and solutions.
Ensures commitments are completed.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Becoming the solution to every problem.
Confusing accountability with control.
Becoming overinvolved in execution.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Role-models accountability in difficult and ambiguous situations and establishes a strong culture of ownership, timely escalation and independent corrective action across the team.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Creates clear ownership.
Encourages early risk reporting.
Builds independent corrective action.
Helps other managers strengthen accountability.
Expert.watchOuts:
Expecting ownership without adequate authority.
Setting unrealistic accountability standards.
Overlooking capability or resource constraints.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Creates confidence by taking responsibility, following through and enabling others to own their work.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: May avoid difficult decisions or retain excessive control, weakening team ownership and confidence.

projects.title: Team Commitment Tracker
projects.whatToDo:
Select 5–8 important team commitments.
Track them for six weeks.
projects.howToDoIt:
Record outcome, owner, due date, status, risk and next action.
Review for 15 minutes each week.
projects.evidence:
Percentage completed on time.
Examples of risks resolved early.

projects.title: Accountability Review
projects.whatToDo: Review one delayed or unsuccessful deliverable.
projects.howToDoIt:
Compare expected and actual outcomes.
Identify what was within the manager’s control.
Define two corrective actions.
projects.evidence:
Completed review note.
Corrective actions implemented.

projects.title: Decision-Ownership Chart
projects.whatToDo: Clarify decisions owned by the manager, employees and reporting manager.
projects.howToDoIt:
Create a one-page decision-rights chart.
Discuss it with the team.
Apply it for four weeks.
projects.evidence:
Fewer unnecessary escalations.
Three decisions independently taken by employees.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: Has limited awareness of emotional triggers and may react visibly during pressure, disagreement or criticism, affecting the quality of interaction and judgement.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Tone may become impatient or defensive.
Personal reactions may influence decisions.
Employees may hesitate to raise concerns.
Developing.watchOuts:
Impulsive reactions.
Visible frustration.
Defensive explanations.
Avoiding difficult situations.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Usually remains composed in routine situations but may struggle to regulate reactions during sustained pressure, criticism or emotionally sensitive conversations.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Regains control after reacting.
Demonstrates awareness of some triggers.
May not recognise the impact of the initial response.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
Suppressing rather than managing emotions.
Inconsistent behaviour under stress.
Delayed recognition of impact.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Recognises and regulates emotions effectively and remains calm, respectful and constructive during pressure, setbacks, disagreement and feedback.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Separates facts from personal reactions.
Receives feedback openly.
Responds proportionately.
Maintains respectful communication.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Appearing emotionally distant.
Overcontrolling emotional expression.
Missing opportunities to show empathy.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Demonstrates exceptional emotional balance in complex and emotionally charged situations and creates stability by helping others remain calm, focused and constructive.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Creates stability during conflict.
Models balanced responses.
Supports others during uncertainty.
Guides other managers in emotional management.
Expert.watchOuts:
Taking responsibility for everyone’s emotions.
Assuming one technique suits everyone.
Becoming the permanent emotional buffer.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Brings calmness and balance to difficult situations, enabling constructive decisions and conversations.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: Emotional reactions or avoidance may affect judgement and discourage employees from raising concerns.

projects.title: Emotional-Trigger Log
projects.whatToDo: Record difficult emotional situations for four weeks.
projects.howToDoIt:
Note the trigger, thought, physical reaction, response and outcome.
Review patterns every Friday.
projects.evidence:
Three common triggers identified.
Planned response for each trigger.

projects.title: Pause-and-Respond Protocol
projects.whatToDo: Apply the protocol in five high-pressure situations.
projects.howToDoIt:
Pause.
Take three slow breaths.
Check facts.
Identify the desired outcome.
Select the response.
projects.evidence:
Five documented examples.
Clear impact on response or outcome.

projects.title: Difficult-Conversation Practice
projects.whatToDo: Conduct three planned difficult conversations.
projects.howToDoIt:
Prepare facts.
Identify likely triggers.
Use neutral language.
Reflect after the conversation.
projects.evidence:
Conversation notes.
Agreed actions.
Observer or manager feedback.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: Relies primarily on familiar methods and may resist feedback or alternative approaches, even when current practices are not producing the required result.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Continues ineffective practices.
Uses the same approach with different employees.
May avoid unfamiliar assignments.
Developing.watchOuts:
Defending current methods.
Viewing feedback as criticism.
Avoiding experimentation.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Accepts feedback and adapts in straightforward situations but may return to familiar habits under pressure or fail to assess whether the new approach was effective.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Tries new approaches when encouraged.
Demonstrates some flexibility.
Does not always evaluate effectiveness.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
Short-lived change.
Superficial adaptation.
Changing without understanding why.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Actively learns from feedback and experience and adjusts the managerial approach according to the situation, employee capability and changing work requirements.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Reflects on outcomes.
Tests alternatives.
Adapts guidance to employee needs.
Sustains effective behavioural changes.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Changing approaches too frequently.
Evaluating new approaches too early.
Creating inconsistency for employees.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Demonstrates high learning agility and converts feedback, experimentation and experience into repeatable practices that improve team effectiveness and support the development of others.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Creates regular learning routines.
Helps employees adapt.
Supports other managers through change.
Shares tested practices.
Expert.watchOuts:
Introducing too many experiments.
Expecting everyone to adapt at the same pace.
Creating change fatigue.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Learns quickly from experience and adjusts the management approach to different people and situations.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: May continue using ineffective approaches or find it difficult to apply feedback consistently.

projects.title: Feedback Sprint
projects.whatToDo: Collect feedback from one manager, two peers and three employees.
projects.howToDoIt:
Ask what to continue, stop and start.
Select two behaviours to practise for six weeks.
projects.evidence:
Feedback summary.
Two behavioural commitments.
Follow-up feedback.

projects.title: Adaptive-Management Experiment
projects.whatToDo: Use different management approaches with two employees.
projects.howToDoIt:
Give one employee greater structure.
Give another greater autonomy.
Review confidence, quality and progress weekly.
projects.evidence:
Comparison of outcomes.
Written learning on when each style works.

projects.title: After-Action Reviews
projects.whatToDo: Review four significant assignments or meetings.
projects.howToDoIt:
Ask what was expected.
Record what happened and why.
Identify what should change next time.
projects.evidence:
Four completed reviews.
Two changes applied to future work.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: Provides broad instructions and may treat most work as equally urgent, resulting in limited clarity around outcomes, ownership and timelines.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Employees may be unclear about priorities.
Roles and standards may remain undefined.
Work may be allocated reactively.
Developing.watchOuts:
Overcommitting the team.
Unclear deadlines.
Frequent unexplained priority changes.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Sets goals and priorities for routine work but may struggle to balance competing demands, dependencies and available team capacity.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Creates basic plans.
Clarifies routine responsibilities.
May overlook trade-offs or workload constraints.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
Planning based on ideal capacity.
Responding to the loudest stakeholder.
Insufficient contingency planning.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Converts team requirements into clear outcomes, priorities, responsibilities, success measures and realistic timelines that guide daily execution.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Employees understand what matters.
Ownership and milestones are clear.
Capacity is considered.
Progress is reviewed regularly.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Overplanning routine work.
Continuing with outdated plans.
Assigning too many priorities.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Establishes strong planning and prioritisation practices and manages complex, competing demands while protecting critical outcomes and maintaining team clarity.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Anticipates dependencies.
Explains trade-offs.
Rebalances capacity proactively.
Helps other managers improve planning.
Expert.watchOuts:
Creating overly complex processes.
Making decisions without team input.
Excessive focus on planning over execution.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Creates clarity and focus by converting requirements into realistic priorities and measurable outcomes.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: Unclear or frequently changing priorities may cause confusion, overwork and missed commitments.

projects.title: 30-Day Team Plan
projects.whatToDo: Plan the team’s key outcomes for one month.
projects.howToDoIt:
List outcomes, milestones, owners, dependencies, risks and measures.
Review every Monday.
projects.evidence:
Completed plan.
Weekly milestone status.
Reprioritisation decisions.

projects.title: Priority-Reset Exercise
projects.whatToDo: Review all current team activities.
projects.howToDoIt:
Classify each as stop, defer, continue or accelerate.
Validate with the reporting manager.
Explain changes to the team.
projects.evidence:
Reduced low-value work.
Clear rationale for revised priorities.

projects.title: Capacity-Planning Board
projects.whatToDo: Map team workload for six weeks.
projects.howToDoIt:
Estimate each employee’s capacity.
Identify overload.
Rebalance work weekly.
projects.evidence:
Lower workload imbalance.
Fewer missed deadlines.
Fewer last-minute reallocations.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: Retains important work or delegates tasks without sufficient clarity, authority or support, resulting in continued dependence on the manager.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Employees may not understand ownership.
Decision authority remains unclear.
Manager becomes a delivery bottleneck.
Developing.watchOuts:
Micromanagement.
Reverse delegation.
Taking work back too quickly.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Delegates routine work but may provide too much or too little oversight because delegation is not consistently matched to employee readiness or assignment risk.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Some employees receive useful independence.
Others experience confusion or control.
Follow-through may be inconsistent.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
Same review approach for every employee.
Insufficient clarity on decision authority.
Delegating mainly low-value tasks.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Delegates meaningful outcomes with clear expectations, authority, resources and proportionate review while allowing employees appropriate independence.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Employees take ownership.
Review is matched to risk and readiness.
Required support is available.
Learning is discussed after completion.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Delegating without checking capability.
Overloading reliable employees.
Intervening too early.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Creates an empowered team and uses delegation deliberately to strengthen delivery, employee capability and independent decision making across the team.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Expands authority progressively.
Creates sustainable ownership practices.
Uses delegation for development.
Helps other managers delegate effectively.
Expert.watchOuts:
Stretching employees without support.
Assuming equal readiness for autonomy.
Delegating only to high performers.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Builds ownership and capability by delegating meaningful work with clear authority and appropriate support.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: May become a bottleneck by retaining work, micromanaging or delegating without sufficient clarity.

projects.title: Delegation Matrix
projects.whatToDo: Identify responsibilities that can move to employees.
projects.howToDoIt:
Record current owner, future owner, authority, support and review frequency.
Transfer three responsibilities.
projects.evidence:
Three completed transfers.
Employee feedback.

projects.title: Staged Delegation
projects.whatToDo: Delegate one moderately complex assignment.
projects.howToDoIt:
Explain outcome and boundaries.
Jointly plan the first stage.
Review at milestones.
Reduce oversight gradually.
projects.evidence:
Assignment completed without being taken back.
Post-task review.

projects.title: Reverse-Delegation Audit
projects.whatToDo: Track issues returned to the manager for two weeks.
projects.howToDoIt: Ask employees to present the issue, two options and a recommendation.
projects.evidence:
More employee-led resolutions.
Reduced upward escalation.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: May act before fully understanding an issue or escalate routine matters unnecessarily, leading to reactive decisions and repeated problems.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Assumptions may replace evidence.
Symptoms may be treated instead of causes.
Routine decisions may be delayed.
Developing.watchOuts:
Jumping to solutions.
Waiting for perfect information.
Escalating to avoid responsibility.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Resolves familiar problems effectively but may struggle when information is incomplete, perspectives differ or consequences are uncertain.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Uses some evidence.
Identifies practical options.
May not consistently compare alternatives.
Does not always review outcomes.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
Confirmation bias.
Reusing old solutions without testing relevance.
Delayed decisions.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Clarifies problems, gathers relevant information and makes timely and practical decisions within authority after considering alternatives and consequences.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Identifies underlying causes.
Involves the right people.
Balances speed and risk.
Reviews decision effectiveness.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Overanalysing low-risk decisions.
Seeking excessive consensus.
Failing to record important decisions.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Handles complex and ambiguous problems effectively and establishes sound problem-solving and decision-making practices that strengthen judgement across the team.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Anticipates recurring problems.
Balances speed, quality and risk.
Coaches employees in analysis.
Helps other managers strengthen judgement.
Expert.watchOuts:
Applying complex methods to simple issues.
Allowing consultation to delay action.
Becoming the only decision-maker.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Makes timely and balanced decisions by clarifying issues, using evidence and considering consequences.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: May make reactive decisions, delay action or escalate issues that should be resolved within the team.

projects.title: Recurring-Problem Project
projects.whatToDo: Select one recurring delay, error or complaint.
projects.howToDoIt:
Define the problem.
Gather data.
Conduct a five-whys analysis.
Test one corrective action.
projects.evidence:
Before-and-after data.
Confirmed reduction or learning.

projects.title: Decision Log
projects.whatToDo: Record six significant decisions.
projects.howToDoIt: Capture issue, evidence, options, risks, decision and result.
projects.evidence:
Completed log.
Two lessons applied later.

projects.title: Problem-Solving Huddles
projects.whatToDo: Conduct four team sessions on real problems.
projects.howToDoIt:
Define the issue.
Analyse causes.
Generate options.
Agree action and owner.
projects.evidence:
Four documented decisions.
Progress against actions.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: Assumes employees understand expectations and monitors performance inconsistently, allowing gaps to continue until they become difficult to address.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Employees may not know required standards.
Performance issues remain unaddressed.
Feedback may come as a surprise.
Developing.watchOuts:
Vague standards.
Avoiding underperformance conversations.
Waiting for formal appraisal cycles.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Sets basic expectations and reviews routine performance but may rely on general impressions or delay corrective action in more difficult situations.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Provides some accountability.
Conducts routine reviews.
May apply standards inconsistently.
May overlook early warning signs.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
Recency bias.
Focusing only on output.
Inconsistent standards.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Sets clear expectations, reviews evidence consistently, recognises effective performance and addresses gaps promptly, fairly and constructively.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Employees know what good performance looks like.
Progress is reviewed regularly.
Effective work is recognised.
Improvement actions are clear.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Assuming every gap is motivational.
Ignoring workload, skill or process issues.
Overformalising routine discussions.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Creates a strong culture of accountability and performance ownership and helps other managers establish fair, evidence-based and developmental performance practices.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Anticipates performance risks.
Tailors support.
Builds employee self-monitoring.
Strengthens performance practices in others.
Expert.watchOuts:
Excessive performance pressure.
Neglecting employee sustainability.
Treating all performance issues identically.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Creates clarity and accountability through fair expectations, evidence-based reviews and timely action.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: Employees may experience unclear standards, inconsistent monitoring or unresolved performance gaps.

projects.title: Performance Rhythm
projects.whatToDo: Introduce a three-month review cycle.
projects.howToDoIt:
Set monthly goals.
Hold fortnightly check-ins.
Conduct monthly reviews.
projects.evidence:
Completed records.
Goal achievement percentage.
Employee feedback.

projects.title: Performance Evidence Sheet
projects.whatToDo: Create a one-page record for each employee.
projects.howToDoIt: Track outcomes, quality, deadlines, behaviours, recognition, support and actions.
projects.evidence:
Discussions supported by examples.
Reduced reliance on impressions.

projects.title: Performance-Improvement Project
projects.whatToDo: Address one recurring performance gap.
projects.howToDoIt:
Clarify expected versus actual performance.
Diagnose the cause.
Agree support and actions.
Review after 30 and 60 days.
projects.evidence:
Measurable improvement.
Documented next step.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: Provides feedback that may be vague, delayed or mainly corrective and tends to solve problems for employees rather than helping them think independently.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Employees may not understand what to repeat.
Required changes may remain unclear.
Independent problem solving remains weak.
Developing.watchOuts:
Personality labels.
Excessive advice.
Avoiding corrective feedback.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Provides useful feedback in routine situations but may avoid sensitive issues, ask too few questions or provide solutions before understanding the employee’s perspective.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Supports immediate correction.
Provides some developmental guidance.
May not build sustained learning.
Follow-through may be inconsistent.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
Moving to solutions too quickly.
Asking too few questions.
Weak follow-through.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Provides timely, specific and balanced feedback and uses thoughtful questions and guidance to support employee ownership, learning and improvement.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Employees understand behaviour and impact.
Improvement actions are clear.
Employees generate possible solutions.
Progress is followed up.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Coaching when direct instruction is needed.
Avoiding accountability.
Overusing structured models.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Role-models high-quality feedback and coaching, handles sensitive conversations skilfully and builds a strong culture of continuous feedback and learning.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Adapts coaching to employee needs.
Develops independent judgement.
Builds coaching capability in other managers.
Normalises regular feedback.
Expert.watchOuts:
Overcoaching routine issues.
Coaching when a clear decision is required.
Creating dependence on coaching conversations.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Accelerates improvement through specific feedback, thoughtful questions and consistent follow-up.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: Feedback may be too vague, delayed or advice-heavy to create sustained employee learning.

projects.title: Weekly Feedback Practice
projects.whatToDo: Give every employee one feedback message per week.
projects.howToDoIt:
Describe the situation, behaviour, impact and desired action.
Ask for the employee’s perspective.
projects.evidence:
Feedback log.
Examples of changed or repeated behaviour.

projects.title: Structured Coaching Conversations
projects.whatToDo: Conduct three 30-minute coaching sessions.
projects.howToDoIt:
Discuss goal, reality, options and way forward.
Ensure employees generate most options.
projects.evidence:
Employee-owned actions.
Progress reviewed within two weeks.

projects.title: Coaching Follow-Through
projects.whatToDo: Select two employees with development goals.
projects.howToDoIt:
Agree one observable behaviour each.
Review fortnightly for eight weeks.
projects.evidence:
Before-and-after examples.
Employee reflection.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: Focuses mainly on immediate delivery and has limited understanding of employee strengths, development needs and career aspirations.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Development is generic.
Formal training is overemphasised.
Opportunities may be distributed unevenly.
Developing.watchOuts:
Developing only high performers.
Treating course attendance as development.
Ignoring career interests.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Identifies basic development needs and provides occasional learning opportunities, but development actions may lack clear goals, support and follow-through.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Employees receive some exposure.
Development may not be individualised.
Application of learning may not be reviewed.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
One-size-fits-all plans.
Assignments without support.
Weak learning reviews.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Understands individual strengths and development gaps and provides relevant work-based learning, exposure, coaching and stretch opportunities with appropriate support.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Development is linked to actual work.
Opportunities reflect individual needs.
Progress is reviewed.
Learning is applied on the job.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Overambitious plans.
Ignoring workload or readiness.
Insufficient support during stretch work.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Creates a strong talent-development environment that builds future capability, knowledge sharing, internal mobility and succession readiness within and beyond the team.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Creates differentiated pathways.
Builds readiness for broader roles.
Encourages knowledge sharing.
Helps other managers develop people.
Expert.watchOuts:
Neglecting current delivery.
Labelling potential too early.
Focusing development on a small group.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Builds capability and motivation by connecting individual needs with practical development opportunities.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: Employees may receive limited, unequal or poorly followed-through development support.

projects.title: Team Capability Matrix
projects.whatToDo: Map the capability of every employee.
projects.howToDoIt:
List critical role skills.
Assess readiness using evidence.
Select one priority per person.
projects.evidence:
Completed matrix.
One active action per employee.

projects.title: Supported Stretch Assignment
projects.whatToDo: Give one employee a responsibility beyond the current role.
projects.howToDoIt:
Define delivery and learning outcomes.
Clarify authority and support.
Review weekly.
projects.evidence:
Completed assignment.
Employee reflection.
Capability improvement.

projects.title: 90-Day Development Plan
projects.whatToDo: Create a development plan with one employee.
projects.howToDoIt:
Use 70% experience.
Use 20% coaching or exposure.
Use 10% formal learning.
Review monthly.
projects.evidence:
Completed activities.
New capability applied at work.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: Communicates mainly through instructions and provides limited context or opportunity for discussion, which may reduce understanding and employee participation.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Employees may not understand the purpose.
Questions may remain unspoken.
Misunderstandings may go unnoticed.
Developing.watchOuts:
One-way communication.
Assuming silence means understanding.
Interrupting employees.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Communicates routine information clearly but may not consistently adapt the message to the audience or listen for underlying questions and concerns.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Basic alignment is achieved.
Routine instructions are understood.
Misunderstandings may continue during change.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
Sharing information late.
Listening only to prepare a response.
Overlooking quieter voices.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Communicates expectations, decisions and context clearly and listens actively to employee views, questions and concerns to ensure shared understanding.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Checks understanding.
Encourages questions.
Adapts communication.
Creates two-way dialogue.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Providing excessive detail.
Losing the central message.
Becoming the only communication channel.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Demonstrates exceptional clarity and listening and establishes effective communication practices that strengthen transparency, alignment and dialogue across teams.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Handles sensitive messages well.
Adapts to different audiences.
Builds open information flow.
Develops communication capability in others.
Expert.watchOuts:
Assuming one style suits everyone.
Becoming overinvolved in employee communication.
Creating unnecessary processes.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Creates alignment and trust through clear, timely communication and attentive listening.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: One-way, unclear or delayed communication may result in misunderstanding and low participation.

projects.title: Team-Meeting Redesign
projects.whatToDo: Improve six consecutive weekly meetings.
projects.howToDoIt:
Cover priorities, progress, decisions, risks, questions and actions.
Rotate employee updates.
projects.evidence:
Documented actions.
Reduced meeting drift.
Employee feedback.

projects.title: Communication Cascade
projects.whatToDo: Translate one organisational priority for the team.
projects.howToDoIt:
Explain why it matters.
Clarify what will change.
Explain individual implications.
Invite questions.
projects.evidence: Employees accurately explain the priority and responsibilities.

projects.title: Listening Interviews
projects.whatToDo: Hold a 20-minute discussion with every employee.
projects.howToDoIt: Ask what supports performance, what creates difficulty and what the manager should change.
projects.evidence:
Summary of recurring themes.
Three visible actions.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: May apply standards inconsistently or make decisions based on personal preference, resulting in perceptions of favouritism or unequal treatment.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Opportunities may be unevenly allocated.
Commitments may not be consistently maintained.
Decision logic may remain unclear.
Developing.watchOuts:
Informal promises.
Inconsistent exceptions.
Sharing confidential information.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Usually treats employees respectfully and fairly but may become inconsistent under pressure or fail to explain the reasoning behind decisions.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Relationships are generally positive.
Standards are usually applied fairly.
Employees may not understand some decisions.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
Treating fairness as identical treatment.
Explaining decisions too late.
Failing to address perceptions of bias.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Builds dependable relationships, keeps commitments and applies standards, opportunities and recognition consistently while accounting for legitimate individual differences.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Decisions are explained.
Confidentiality is maintained.
Opportunities are allocated fairly.
Concerns are handled respectfully.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Making promises that cannot be fulfilled.
Avoiding necessary differentiation.
Overexplaining confidential decisions.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Role-models ethical, inclusive and transparent leadership and creates a psychologically safe environment characterised by fairness, openness and respectful treatment.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Employees raise concerns early.
Mistakes are discussed constructively.
Access to opportunities is monitored.
Other managers learn from these practices.
Expert.watchOuts:
Treating trust as a substitute for accountability.
Promising complete transparency.
Avoiding controls in the name of empowerment.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Builds commitment by treating employees consistently, keeping commitments and making transparent decisions.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: Perceived inconsistency or favouritism may reduce trust, openness and employee confidence.

projects.title: Fairness Audit
projects.whatToDo: Review work, recognition, visibility and development allocation.
projects.howToDoIt:
Compare distribution across employees.
Identify unexplained imbalances.
Take corrective action.
projects.evidence:
Completed audit.
Documented reallocation or rationale.

projects.title: Decision-Transparency Practice
projects.whatToDo: Explain four significant team decisions.
projects.howToDoIt:
State criteria, evidence, constraints and trade-offs.
Invite questions.
projects.evidence:
Four decision notes.
Improved employee understanding.

projects.title: Team Norms Charter
projects.whatToDo: Agree 5–7 behavioural norms.
projects.howToDoIt:
Discuss respect, confidentiality, participation, mistakes and disagreement.
Review monthly.
projects.evidence:
Published charter.
Examples of norms used.

Developing.proficiencyDescription: Avoids disagreement, delays intervention or reacts personally to tension, allowing relatively minor issues to become recurring relationship or performance problems.
Developing.behaviouralImplications:
Issues may remain unresolved.
Tension may spread across the team.
Employees may lose confidence in the manager.
Developing.watchOuts:
Discussing the issue with others.
Aggressive responses.
Excessive accommodation.

Intermediate.proficiencyDescription: Handles straightforward disagreements but may struggle when emotions are strong, positions are fixed or the issue requires sustained follow-through.
Intermediate.behaviouralImplications:
Facilitates basic discussion.
Restores temporary cooperation.
May not address underlying issues.
Follow-through may be weak.
Intermediate.watchOuts:
Accepting superficial agreement.
Prioritising immediate harmony.
Delaying necessary escalation.

Proficient.proficiencyDescription: Addresses conflict early, listens to different perspectives and resolves issues calmly and directly by focusing on facts, behaviour, impact and future action.
Proficient.behaviouralImplications:
Issues are raised early.
Different views are heard.
Clear actions are agreed.
Follow-up is completed.
Proficient.watchOuts:
Managing serious misconduct without support.
Becoming the permanent mediator.
Ignoring policy or HR requirements.

Expert.proficiencyDescription: Role-models mature conflict resolution and creates a culture in which disagreement is raised early, handled respectfully and used to improve decisions and working relationships.
Expert.behaviouralImplications:
Handles emotionally charged conflict.
Identifies underlying interests.
Builds constructive challenge.
Develops conflict capability in others.
Expert.watchOuts:
Normalising harmful conflict.
Mediating issues employees should resolve.
Delaying decisive intervention.

reportContent.strengthStatement: Protects relationships and performance by addressing disagreements early, calmly and constructively.
reportContent.developmentNeedStatement: Avoided or poorly handled conflict may create recurring tension, low collaboration and loss of trust.

projects.title: Current-Conflict Resolution
projects.whatToDo: Select one genuine team disagreement.
projects.howToDoIt:
Meet each person separately.
Clarify facts and impact.
Facilitate a joint discussion.
Agree actions.
projects.evidence:
Written agreement.
Named owners.
Two-week follow-up.

projects.title: Conflict-Pattern Review
projects.whatToDo: Analyse three previous conflicts.
projects.howToDoIt:
Identify triggers, assumptions, delayed actions and response patterns.
Define preventive actions.
projects.evidence:
Personal conflict-risk checklist.
Checklist used in one new situation.

projects.title: Constructive-Challenge Process
projects.whatToDo: Introduce a method for discussing opposing views.
projects.howToDoIt:
Ask participants to state the issue, facts, impact, alternative view and recommendation.
Pilot it in three meetings.
projects.evidence:
Three documented discussions.
Decisions reached without personal conflict.
